items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had never heard an orchestra like the Synco Septette. ... McKinney, who was a drummer, had stopped playing drums and was the business manager for the orchestra. I knew Nesbit and the other members we met that night.

ctx.x: This orchestra had a very big name but it had never come to Cincinnati so Helvey and a few other members of the orchestra including myself decided to go to Dayton to hear the McKinney orchestra.

We made the trip in Helvey's 5-passenger model T Ford. Dayton was 50 miles from Cincy and it was a trip well worth taking because I had never heard an orchestra like the Synco Septette. John Nesbitt had joined this group when he left Cincinnati. McKinney, who was a drummer, had stopped playing drums and was the business manager for the orchestra. I knew Nesbit and the other members we met that night. Cuba Austin was the drummer, Todd Rhodes, piano, Dave Wilborn, banjo, Claude Jones, trombone, Milton Senior,…

The Synco Septette were a show band and dance orchestra combined and they were the first and only negro orchestra that I've ever seen with the high quality of musicianship and showmanship that they possessed. I remember seeing a white show band on stage at a theatre in Louisville, Kentucky, the first time I went to that city with Helvey, and I remember them doing a tune called "Sunday" which is a standard tune today. I had also seen other white show bands in some theatres in Cincy and they were always good. But…
